title: Permian micro-balance
as_of_note: Current frame on the EIA October 2026 STEO path. Items carry their own vintages; the production split items are older or unmeasured, and say so on the item.
units: kb/d unless a field name says otherwise

supply.label: Delaware Basin, Texas production
supply.source: Texas RRC production by county (not held)
supply.note: Reeves and Loving counties anchor the item (363 and 404 kb/d, Novi Labs 2025, medium-low confidence). The county pull does not exist in the library, so no current value is printed.

supply.label: Delaware Basin, New Mexico production
supply.source: Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Permian Basin page
supply.note: Lea plus Eddy counties, 2.1 MMb/d combined at Q4 2024 (Lea 1.2, Eddy 0.9). The last hard official split; New Mexico was growing about six times faster than Texas Permian at that reading, so the share has likely risen since.

supply.label: Midland Basin production
supply.source: Texas RRC production by county (not held)
supply.note: Martin and Midland counties anchor the item (593 and 559 kb/d, Novi Labs 2025, medium-low confidence). No official Midland versus Delaware production split exists in public data at any current vintage.

supply.label: Central Basin Platform and other Permian production
supply.source: Texas RRC production by county (not held)
supply.note: Winkler, Ector, Crane and fringe counties. Small, a few hundred kb/d in total; the one Winkler figure found (about 68 kb/d) is unverified.

supply.label: Storage change and other receipts (named residual)
supply.source: No Permian-grain storage series is published
supply.note: Midland hub storage is about 20 MMbbl of capacity (RBN, 2024). PADD 3 stocks are the nearest published series and are held in the library. The residual prints as its own line when a flow layer exists; today there is none.

demand.label: Wink to Webster
demand.note: Includes Enterprise's 29 percent undivided interest segment (Midland-to-ECHO 3). Never add a full Midland-to-ECHO system on top of this line.

demand.label: Midland-to-ECHO 1
demand.note: 575 kb/d in May 2018, raised to 620 in March 2019.

demand.label: Midland-to-ECHO 3 (undivided interest share)
demand.note: Enterprise's roughly 450 kb/d undivided-interest share of the Wink to Webster steel. Counted inside Wink to Webster above, not additive. The Seminole line (Midland-to-ECHO 2) reportedly returned to crude in late 2025 for about 200 kb/d of swing; unverified against an Enterprise primary source, so it is carried here as a watch note, not capacity.

demand.label: BridgeTex
demand.note: Ran about 20 percent utilised in 2023 after Occidental's exit, recovered to about 68 percent by May 2024, and cut its committed tariff 27 percent in July 2025 to attract barrels. Utilisation is pipe-specific, not basin arithmetic.

demand.label: Longhorn
demand.note: Reversed products line in crude service since 2013. Frequently omitted from Permian to Houston lists; included here.

demand.label: Gray Oak
demand.note: 900 kb/d at start-up, plus 80 in May 2025 and 40 in May 2026 on drag-reducing agent. East Daley's demo showed a demand read near 1,096 on this line, above the expanded capacity: their demand items are nominations, not metered flow.

demand.label: Cactus II
demand.note: Plains 70 percent (operator), Enbridge 30 percent. Built to the full 670; full service Q1 2020.

demand.label: Cactus III (ex-EPIC)
demand.source: Plains releases and 8-K; East Daley, August 2026
demand.note: Plains acquired 100 percent in 2025. A 75 kb/d expansion came online at the end of August 2026 to reach 725. Expansion toward 900 is unsanctioned optionality.

demand.label: Cactus I
demand.dest: Corpus Christi via the Eagle Ford JV line
demand.note: Origin capacity at McCamey. Corpus delivery rides a joint tariff over the Plains and Enterprise Eagle Ford JV pipeline (660 total), shared with Eagle Ford volumes.

demand.label: Permian Express (system)
demand.note: Phases 1 to 4 overlap and must never be summed. Platts listed 640 in 2022; the system figure used here is about 600.

demand.label: West Texas Gulf
demand.source: Dated trade sources; current rating unverified
demand.note: Built 1952-53. RBN reports Permian Express plus West Texas Gulf together at nearly 1 MMb/d to Nederland, with this line frequently running above its dated nameplate. Carried as a flagged range until a primary source fixes the current rating.

demand.label: Basin Pipeline (Colorado City to Cushing)
demand.note: Segment figure. The Wink to Midland segment of the same system is 600 and is intra-Permian feed, not Cushing throughput.

demand.label: Sunrise system
demand.note: 500 kb/d is Midland to Wichita Falls only. Onward Wichita Falls to Cushing capacity is about 220, and EIA credited Sunrise with only about 120 of incremental Permian to Cushing takeaway. The onward leg is the bottleneck.

demand.label: Centurion to Cushing
demand.source: Historical segment figures; current rating unverified
demand.note: Centurion's system totals (720, and about 1,500 in some profiles) are gathering-inclusive and are not takeaway. Carried at its historical segment range, flagged, until the Form 6 parse fixes a real number.

demand.label: Big Spring refinery (Delek)
demand.note: The only refinery physically inside the Midland Basin proper. An expansion to 100 is reported planned, not in service.

demand.label: El Paso refinery (Marathon)
demand.note: Western edge of the basin's refining demand.

demand.label: Crude by rail, truck and other outflows
demand.source: EIA crude by rail (held, PADD grain)
demand.note: No current published Permian-specific figure. EIA crude-by-rail is held at PADD grain; a Permian attribution is a build-time allocation, not a print.

groups.note: Texas and New Mexico Delaware counties together.

groups.note: All water-bound corridors. Midland-to-ECHO 3 is counted once, inside Wink to Webster.

groups.label: Cushing corridor
groups.source: Group definitions per permian_dossier.md section 8 (overlapping roll-ups, not a partition)
groups.note: Effective takeaway about 710 to 745, far below the segment nameplate sum; the onward legs bottleneck.

groups.label: In-basin demand
groups.source: Group definitions per permian_dossier.md section 8 (overlapping roll-ups, not a partition)
groups.note: 306 of refining capacity inside the basin; under 5 percent of production.

prices.label: WTI Midland minus WTI Cushing
prices.source: Argus prints via public filings and reports
prices.note: A small premium across 2024-25 prints: +$0.35 to +$1.22/bbl. No public 2026 assessed series exists; the assessments are paywalled.

prices.label: MEH minus WTI Midland
prices.note: About $0.20 to $0.50/bbl in 2024-25, spiking on Houston-leg outages (a $1.41 print in the June 2024 trade month during a Wink to Webster outage).

prices.label: WTI Midland assessment
prices.source: Argus and Platts assessments (licensed, not held)
prices.note: The Midland price itself is a licensed assessment. The spreads above are the public-print layer.

storage.source: RBN Energy, Center of the Universe (Midland hub storage)
storage.note: Midland hub tank capacity only. No Permian-grain stock level is published; PADD 3 stocks are the nearest series and are held in the library.

corridors.label: Midland to Houston
corridors.note: Corridor utilisation about 91.7 percent (East Daley 2026, from Texas RRC T-1 filings). The MEH minus Midland spread prices this pull.

corridors.label: Midland to Corpus Christi
corridors.from: Orla, Wink, Crane and McCamey, Texas
corridors.note: Corridor utilisation about 99.7 percent (East Daley 2026, from T-1 filings): the tightest corridor in the basin.

corridors.label: Midland to Nederland
corridors.note: Mostly refining demand, not exports: Nederland area exports ran only about 230 to 250 in October 2025 (RBN).

corridors.label: Midland to Cushing
corridors.note: Corridor utilisation about 68.2 percent (East Daley 2026). Cushing is the relief valve: it holds the basin's spare capacity because the Gulf pays better.

notes: Two-speed system: the basin's spare pipe capacity sits on the corridor barrels least want (Cushing, about 68 percent utilised), while the corridors to the water run nearly full (Corpus about 99.7 percent, Houston about 91.7 percent, East Daley 2026 from Texas RRC T-1 filings). A single basin utilisation number hides the story, so none is printed.

Supply card: 6,900 is the current point on EIA's October 2026 STEO path (2026 average forecast 6,810; Q4 2026 forecast 6,920). It is a control total. The item list does not foot to it (valued items sum 2,100): three of the four production split items are unmeasured at current vintage because no official split exists, and the fourth is a Q4 2024 reading. The difference is the unallocated remainder, named here rather than plugged into an item.

Nameplate card: 7,890 is East Daley's 2026 long-haul reference print from T-1 filings. Bottom-up verified steel in the dossier sums to about 7,200 to 7,400 plus local refining. The gap sits in the unverified zone (West Texas Gulf's current rating, Centurion's Cushing segment, Seminole swing treatment) and is a research finding, not an error to force closed. Their demo frame printed 8,200 nameplate and 8,200 effective.

Effective capacity is not printed as one number: the derate is corridor-specific. Cushing's effective takeaway is about 710 to 745 against segment nameplates that sum far higher, because onward legs bottleneck (Sunrise) and one segment is unverified (Centurion). Corpus and Houston run at nameplate.

Demand card is blank on purpose. No demand item carries a flow, because the Texas RRC T-1 monthly reports, the flow source behind East Daley's utilisation prints, are not held. The last published flow split (RBN, Q1 2025, on about 6,600 of production) was Corpus about 2,500, Houston about 2,400, Nederland about 900, and Cushing plus local plus other about 800. Items carry verified capacity, labelled capacity.

Double-count rules carried on the items: Midland-to-ECHO 3 is steel inside Wink to Webster; Sunrise's 500 ends at Wichita Falls; Centurion's system totals are gathering, not takeaway; Cactus has no Permian-to-Cushing leg.

Price vintage warning: EIA's Permian forecast flipped during 2026. The January 2026 STEO (WTI assumed $52) forecast a plateau at 6.6 falling to 6.5; the October 2026 STEO (WTI realised about $84 through August) forecasts 6.81 in 2026 and 7.14 in 2027. This feed uses the October vintage and says so.

What actually binds crude here is associated gas, not crude pipe. Gas-oil ratios run about 4,200 cubic feet per barrel and climb as wells age. Waha was negative on 46 percent of 2024 trading days. Documented 2026 high-GOR shut-ins run 200 to 400 MMcf/d of gas on any given day (Bloomberg, June 2026); no source converts that to a crude loss, and none is printed. Produced water binds locally under the RRC's seismic response area suspensions and June 2025 disposal guidelines; it is a slow squeeze, not yet a basin-wide cap.

WTI Midland sits inside the Dated Brent basket (since June 2023 deliveries), so Permian barrels loaded at Corpus and Houston help set the world's benchmark price. The export pull is structural, not an afterthought.

No new greenfield long-haul crude pipeline out of the Permian was announced or sanctioned in 2025-2026. All egress growth is brownfield (Gray Oak +120, Cactus III +75) plus one reported, unverified conversion back to crude (Seminole).
